newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere, bank surges in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere, bank surges in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere continued a long-awaited surge on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Friday, breaking a 20-month barrier of $12.5 in hefty demand.
Banque Audi also continued a spectacular six-month climb, jumping to a record $28.5 on news that it had bought Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient bank.
The LIBX bank index climbed 0.64 percent to 180.42. The LISPI general index rose 0.92 percent to 93.99 and the BLOM general index increased 3.44 percent to 1074.75.
Market turnover was 354,420 shares for a value of $4,743,022 against Thursday's 349,626 shares for a value of $4,142,740.
Thursday's news that Solidere planned to open up share ownership to foreign investors in October fuelled the surge by the company's A and B shares.
Both jumped $0.50, boosting a demand-driven climb that began at the start of the week.
Demand for Solidere on Friday's first fixing totalled 630,952 shares against supply of 186,015. All supply orders at the two fixings, totalling 242,973 shares, were executed.
Equally spectacular was Banque Audi's $0.875 surge to a record $28.5 from Thursday's $27.625 -- 90 percent above its $15 issue price last January.

Audi on Thursday announced the acquisition for $50 million of medium-sized Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient which has assets of $253 million, a 0.85 percent market share and eight branches in Lebanon.
Banque Audi's global depositary receipts traded at $29.5 on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange on Friday.
Of the two other listed banks, Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $4.5 in strong demand and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell to $20.75 from $21.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
